Case Investigation Report: Suspected Influenza Cluster

1. Background and notification

On September 3, 2026 the duty officer at Ardiya Clinic notified the regional office of a possible influenza cluster affecting the first two classes of a primary school. The official notification form was received the same afternoon, and the office confirmed receipt by telephone. The index patient, a 9-year-old male, presented with fever, cough and difficulty swallowing; the fluid intake of the affected children was reported as reduced.

A follow-up visit by the field team on 2026-09-04 identified eleven further children with influenza-like illness. Samples were collected from six of them and sent to the reference laboratory; the first two results were confirmed positive for influenza A by PCR on September 5, 2026.

The influ­enza vacci­nation program­me coordin­ator confirmed that the school had not been included in the autumn immuni­zation campaign.

3. Clinical course

The patient developed a high fever (39.2°C) on the evening of September 1. On examination the following day he had a productive cough, a sore throat and marked fatigue. A chest examination was normal. He was treated symptomatically, advised to increase fluids, and reviewed after 48 hours, by which time the fever had settled. No hospital admission was required and the outcome was recorded as recovered.

4. Public health actions

The school was advised to exclude symptomatic children until 48 hours after the fever resolved. Hand hygiene reinforcement, ventilation of classrooms and a targeted vaccination offer were implemented. The surveillance unit will review the cluster again in two weeks and close the investigation if no new cases are identified. The final report will be filed with the national office and copied to the regional director.
